title: ELF string tables can reference suffixes of existing strings
summary: A string table index is a byte offset from the head of the table that can point inside another string and share a trailing NUL.
applies: ELF file; System V Common ABI
detail: If the table contains foobar plus the terminating byte, the offset to b can legally represent bar.
boundary: Before interpreting st_name and other fields, the associated string table must be selected first; the same offset in different tables does not matter.
relevance: Explains the case where the index does not point to the first enumerated boundary of the string, but still gives a valid name.
